description: Curated parameter library for the ice pressure-area relation p = p0*A**-ex, one record per primary/derived source. Every record declares units, area definition, geometry of the loaded footprint, test/rule conditions and the evidence class, so that an exponent can never be quoted without its area convention.
reading_discipline: primary_source_verified=false means the primary document could not be opened in this build environment (no network egress). The number is a literature value, not a transcription of the standard.
role=regression_anchor records this repository's own transcription and may only detect drift, never serve as external truth.
an exponent is only consumable together with its area_definition; see src/tensorphysics/ice_pressure_area/conventions.py.
no value in this file is measured inside this repository; the in-repo records (evidence_class=repo_transcription) exist to expose contradictions between our own artifacts.

entries.citation: Sanderson, T.J.O. (1988) Ice Mechanics: Risks to Offshore Structures. Graham & Trotman, London. Global ice pressure-area relation p = C*A**-0.3 with C = 0.7 MPa at A = 1 m2 (as reproduced in Masterson & Frederking 1993, Cold Reg. Sci. Technol. 21:169-185)
entries.verification_note: Monograph not accessible offline. The exponent 0.30 and prefactor 0.7 MPa are the canonical global-pressure line as reproduced in the secondary literature; the prefactor magnitude carries a factor ~1.5 scatter between compilations and must not be used as a design datum.
entries.notes: Global (structure-scale) pressure: the area is the nominal structure area over which the total ice load is averaged, not a contact patch.

entries.citation: Masterson, D.M. & Frederking, R.M.W. (1993) Local contact pressures in ship/ice and structure/ice interactions. Cold Regions Science and Technology 21(2):169-185. Local pressure-area envelope p = p0*A**-0.7 over nominal contact areas of indenters and ship panels
entries.verification_note: Compilation not accessible offline. Exponent 0.70 with a band 0.55-0.80 is the upper (conservative) local pressure-area envelope quoted for small contact areas; the paper's data scatter is the reason for the wide band. The prefactor is not transcribed.
entries.notes: Upper envelope of local contact pressure vs nominal contact area; representative of the 'local' end of the pressure-area family.

entries.citation: ISO 19906:2010 Petroleum and natural gas industries - Arctic offshore structures, Annex A (global and local ice actions), pressure-area form p = p0*A**-ex with ex = 0.45 for first-year ice; as transcribed in TensorPhysics src/tensorphysics/ice_plasticity/iso19906.py::typical_ice_belt_params
entries.verification_note: ISO 19906 is paywalled and was not opened. ex = 0.45 and p0 = 3.0 MPa are this repository's transcription (ice_plasticity/iso19906.py); the 0.40-0.55 band is literature scatter, not a clause value. This record is the one GAP-PP-2 must eventually re-verify against the standard.
entries.notes: Nominal contact area of the load patch; aspect ratio 4:1 follows the IACS patch geometry already used by the plate-buckling line of this repository.

entries.citation: IACS Unified Requirement I2 (Polar Class hull structures, Rev. 2016) local ice pressure on shell plating p = p0*A**-0.45, applied at PC6 with p0 = 2.5 MPa at A = 1 m2; transcribed in TensorPhysics benchmarks/ice_nav_refs/assets/iacs_ur_i_pc6.json::IACS_PC6_PANEL_PRESSURE_TABLE
entries.verification_note: UR I2 could not be downloaded in the build environment; the pressure-area form is public and reproduced, the class reference pressure is a 2.0-3.0 MPa band. Must be re-verified before scantling use.

data_points.note: the sha256-anchored asset values; used to check that the fit in this library recovers the declared exponent

entries.notes: Second independent rule-form record of ex = 0.45 for the nominal patch area; agrees with the ISO 19906 record, which is why the design-rule stratum can be pooled.

entries.citation: Johnston, M.E., Frederking, R.M.W., Timco, G.W. & Sodhi, D.S. (1998) Pressure-area relationships from medium-scale ice indentation tests. IAHR Ice Symposium, Potsdam. Medium-scale field indentation of first-year sea ice at Hobson's Choice Ice Island
entries.verification_note: Proceedings not accessible offline. Exponent 0.55 with band 0.45-0.65 is the medium-scale field indentation value quoted in review compilations for nominal (indenter) contact area, cold first-year ice, with the test's own scatter as band width.
entries.notes: The only record in the library that carries an ice-temperature range, which is why the temperature meta-regression is rank-deficient (see calibration report).

entries.citation: TensorPhysics src/tensorphysics/ice_modules/local_pressure.py (LocalPressureModel.exponent = -0.15, P0_MPa = 14.0, docstring attribute: IACS Unified Interpretation I, Rev.3 2016) - in-repository transcription, verified in-tree
entries.verification_note: Verified in-tree: the exponent -0.15 and the 14.0 MPa reference pressure are literally present in local_pressure.py. Whether IACS UR I actually prescribes ex = 0.15 is NOT established (document inaccessible); the record exists because it contradicts IACS_UR_I2_PC6_PATCH_PRESSURE (ex = 0.45) inside this same repository.
entries.notes: Defect record: same family label as the corpus asset, exponent 3x smaller. The library's conflict detector must flag this pair.

entries.citation: TensorPhysics src/tensorphysics/ice_modules/local_pressure.py::FREDERKSON_REF (5 tabulated average pressures 14.0/10.8/9.5/7.8/6.8 MPa at A = 1/5/10/25/50 m2, labelled 'Frederikson (2006) model tests', 'Calibrated to match IACS UR I pressure-area law') - in-repository transcription, verified in-tree
entries.verification_note: Verified in-tree: the five tabulated values are literally present in local_pressure.py. Their provenance is a self-declared calibration to the -0.15 law, i.e. a regression anchor, not a measured dataset.

data_points.note: declared ex of this table is 0.185 (log-space fit performed by this library); the model that consumes it uses 0.15 - a 23 % internal inconsistency recorded here on purpose

entries.notes: Regression anchor for the in-repo IACS model table.
